//: One source of truth for the per-plugin CI lanes. Read by integrations/tooling/lanes.mjs, which .github/workflows/ci.yml and integrations/tooling/run-lane.mjs both go through. See integrations/PARALLEL_LANES.md.
sharedIndexNote: Port block for the CI jobs that are not a plugin lane — the hosting-surface check and the generic plugin-system e2e suite. A reserved index rather than a separate fixed block, so there is one port formula and lanes.test.mjs can prove it collides with nothing. No lane may take index 9.

lanes.note: OCM 1.5 receiver: discovery, JWK Set, RFC 9421 (tag=ocm) signed shares and notifications, the shared file fetched into the blob store, SHARE_ACCEPTED sent back. The e2e runs at --plugin-routes read-write against an invented OCM peer fixture (e2e/peer.mjs, HTTPS on loopback with a throwaway test CA), which the debug-build seams in serverEnv let the server reach. Needs an .atomic-server-ref with atomic-server branch claude/plugin-ocm-host (OCM key discovery, tagged signing, JWKs, blobs.fetch, on top of claude/plugin-fediverse-host for the seams, and the route field `fetches` of pin candidate16); pin candidate16 (38306758) has all of them, and the e2e passed there on 2026-09-29; it fails at a pin without them. No interoperability claim with a real Nextcloud/ownCloud peer.

e2e installs the Calendar drive app from the catalog (Integrations, Drive apps; the dev-server serves the committed apps/calendar/<version>/ui.js in place of GitHub Pages) and drives it in its plugin iframe: connect through the host's consent bar, choose a calendar, import and refresh through the host proxy relay, then preview and send edits with If-Match (atomic-server#1657's ifMatch, in the pin), against the mock proxy's stateful google-calendar fixture and its test drivers.

A remoteStorage server (draft-dejong-remotestorage-22) on the installation-origin mount. The e2e runs atomic-server built with the plugin-routes feature at --plugin-routes read-write: server.spec.ts installs the unchanged bundle through the store's review dialog and drives remotestorage.js (npm remotestoragejs, pinned in e2e/package.json) through WebFinger, the host consent page and the storage API; import.spec.ts runs the reviewed text importer through /plugin-run. Needs a host with authOptional bearer routes, trailing-slash {*rest} matches redirects to a consented client and handler CORS expose headers (atomic-server branch claude/plugin-remotestorage-host, on candidate14); the node tier needs no server.

paths: devonian/github-issues/ imports the devonian package from source (vitest.config.ts aliases it to devonian/src/main.ts), so a devonian change runs this lane too. Its tests ran in devonian CI before the lens moved here. The e2e installs the GitHub issues drive app (app/, npm devonian from app/package.json) from the catalog's Drive apps section, as the committed apps/issue-tracker/<version>/ui.js, and drives it through the host's proxy relay (atomic-server#1657, in the pin) against the mock proxy's seeded atomic-fixture/tracker repository.

Solid pod on an installation origin: LDP resources and containers as PlainText atoms, Turtle/JSON-LD, N3 Patch and SPARQL Update data, strong ETags, WAC-Allow, Solid-OIDC DPoP verified by the host (`auth: dpop`, atomic-server claude/plugin-solid-host). The e2e starts a test Solid-OIDC issuer on the lane's otherwise unused mock-proxy port (platforms is empty) and drives the pod with @inrupt/solid-client; against a host without `auth: dpop` it skips with that reason.

Node: QuickJS handle-to-DID and did:web document route checks and a reproducible bundle. e2e: publishes plugin.mjs to atomic-server built with the plugin-routes feature at --plugin-routes read-only, binds two invented host names to the test drive, installs with a did:web identity and resolves /.well-known/atproto-did and /.well-known/did.json on the handle host over HTTP with a Host header (no TLS, DNS or network). Where the host reports hostFeatures.pluginRoutes.requestHost (atomic-server claude/plugin-atproto-host), the other host name must answer 404; otherwise the spec records that every host name of the drive answers. No independent resolver library or live Bluesky verification.

e2e drives the Bank statements importer through the host's generic file entry point (atomic-server#1653: manifest accepts/destination, PluginPage Import tab): publish, discover, set up, MT940 and camt.053 import, reload, reimport, local edit, conflict and refused files. A second test installs the Money drive app (integrations/money/app/) test-side as an app rendering the Bank transaction class, adds it through the table's Add view as a read-only view, imports an MT940 from inside the app through the host's review (store.importer.run, atomic-server#1774), and saves a category after the host's Allow editing (atomic-server#1788). The pin includes that change (atomic-server#1691); against an older host, publishing the bundle fails on the unknown manifest field. Host bug atomic-server#1846, fixed at pin 1432e244a (atomic-server#1847, atomic-plugins #179): at pin 2567fc30b Add view read the drive's apps once on mount, so when the app's save synced in after navigating, 'New app' never appeared and the second test failed. No typecheck/unit tier: money has an atomicCertification block, so the unsharded certification step in shared-checks already runs exactly its typecheck (tsconfig.json) and unit (vitest.config.ts) on every integrations/** change, plus bundle reproducibility. moneybird is listed for a future Moneybird fixture in integrations/money/fixtures/moneybird/ (plugin-specific files stay in the plugin folder); integrations/money/ has no Moneybird runtime code.

node: the handler's decisions against an in-memory host (projection, WebFinger, NodeInfo, publish, Follow/Accept, Undo, replies, Delete) and bundle reproducibility. e2e: the bundle on atomic-server built with plugin-routes at read-write, federating with the ActivityPub peer fixture in integrations/fediverse/e2e/peer.ts (HTTPS on loopback, self-signed): WebFinger and NodeInfo through /.well-known/, a host-verified signed Follow answered by a signed Accept from the host delivery queue, a publish over auth: atomic delivered as a signed Create, a reply stored as an Atomic Message, and Undo. The e2e needs atomic-server branch claude/plugin-fediverse-host (auth: atomic, request.caller.actor, WebFinger rels, and the debug-build ATOMIC_PLUGIN_E2E_LOOPBACK_PEERS and ATOMIC_PLUGIN_E2E_PEER_CA seams that serverEnv turns on: loopback peers, with the peer's throwaway test CA as the only trusted root there); at a pin without it, the e2e tier fails.

The e2e installs the Notion drive app (integrations/notion/app/) from the catalog's Drive apps section, as the committed apps/notion/<version>/ui.js, and drives it through the host's integration-proxy relay (store.proxy, consent bar and connect return) from ontola/atomic-server#1657, against the shared mock proxy's notion fixture. The live tier stubs fetch in-process.

Willow25 Entry codecs, unsigned signing-candidate job, and the drop route: `GET /_routes/<slug>/willow.drop` answers selected public resources as a Willow drop whose entries the host signs with the installation's Ed25519 subspace key (communal namespace, no delegations). The node tier decodes our drops with the willow-drop importer bundle, which verifies every signature and WILLIAM3 digest. The e2e tier runs at --plugin-routes read-write and needs atomic-server's Willow key bindings, ctx.willow and bodyBase64 (branch claude/plugin-willow-host, not yet in the pin); it fails on a host without them. No WGPS, owned namespaces, delegations or live peer.

e2e installs the Pets drive app from the catalog (Integrations, Drive apps; the committed apps/pets/<version>/ui.js), updates it from an older recorded version, and drives it in its plugin iframe: connect through the host's consent bar and the mock proxy, then import through the host proxy relay (#52). It needs an .atomic-server-ref that includes the relay (atomic-server#1657, for #1624, merged into feat/plugin-debug; the pin has it); against an older pin the app reports that the host cannot reach the proxy and the spec fails at 'Not connected'.

RDF interchange between Atomic snapshots and NextGraph documents. The node tier tests the plugin module. The e2e tier runs the committed plugin in the server QuickJS sandbox, on atomic-server built with plugin-routes and started at read-write with --plugin-sidecars nextgraph=<the lane sidecar port>, against the operator sidecar in integrations/nextgraph/sidecar/ (a real NextGraph wallet and local verifier, built with docker). It needs a host with atomic-sidecar: operations (atomic-server branch claude/plugin-nextgraph-host) that signs its sidecar requests as the installation app agent (atomic-server pin candidate17, pending); on a host without either the spec is skipped with that reason. No NextGraph broker (ngd) is involved: sync between brokers is not verified.

The e2e installs the timesheets drive app from the catalog (Integrations, Drive apps; the committed apps/timesheets/<version>/ui.js) and drives it in its plugin iframe: connect through the host's consent bar and the mock proxy, set up workspace and look-back in the frame, then import, reload, refresh and recover from a proxy failure through the host relay (atomic-server#1657; the pin has it). Provider changes and failures go through the mock proxy's local-only fixture driver (POST /__fixture/clockify). It also checks an M2 conflict and not-loaded time in the #89 views. The old upstream Clockify tests were deleted in atomic-server 4bab16ee6 with the UI they drove (#44).

Willow drop importer (#139), a sandbox job like money: no provider, so no mock proxy (platforms is empty). typecheck and unit are lane tiers rather than certify.mjs's, because certification requires named atomic-server sandbox tests that do not exist for this package; the unit tier also checks that the committed plugin.js is a fresh esbuild bundle. The e2e publishes the bundle and imports fixture drops through the host's generic file entry point (atomic-server#1653, in the pin), so the QuickJS sandbox runs the Ed25519 and WILLIAM3 code and a binary file crosses the text-only hand-over. The fixtures come from willow25 (fixtures/generate/), which CI does not run.

A tooling lane (#134), not a plugin: it lives in integrations/tooling/ (`dir`) and runs only when one of its `paths` changes, not on every tooling or shared change, because each run builds atomic-server with the feature (or pulls its image). Its node tests run in shared-checks like every tooling test. It tests the gates of docs/design/server-plugin-routes.md section 0 against atomic-server built with the `plugin-routes` feature (atomic-server#1726, #1732). pluginRoutes runs the e2e twice, first at `--plugin-routes read-only`, then at `off`, on a fresh server over the same store. The spec publishes the gated fixture plugin (integrations/tooling/fixtures/gated-plugin/) and checks the `requires` and `hostFeatures` /plugin-catalog reports. At read-only it pins it, installs it through the store's review dialog and requests its drive-prefix route, which answers the fixture's body. At off, pinning is refused with host-feature-unavailable, the review dialog's Install button is disabled, and the installation from the read-only run, now degraded, answers 404. Needs an .atomic-server-ref with atomic-server#1726, #1732, #1749 and #1751.

A tooling lane (#177), not a plugin: it runs only when the shared ontology (ontology/, ontology-kit/), the dev-server that serves it, or the pin changes. Its node tests (ontology-kit/*.test.mjs) run in shared-checks. The e2e checks that the pinned host reads a generated class (event-v1) from the dev-server's /ontology/ path, which serves the committed term files with their subjects moved to its own origin and GitHub Pages' headers, and that atomic-server accepts a hand-made table of that class and a row with one of its properties. With ATOMIC_SERVER_IMAGE set the spec uses host.docker.internal, so the server in Docker fetches the same URL as the browser.
